item: A test that leaves its own stand-in on the process-wide socket calls fails by name; the event-loop test server starts with the default SIGINT handler
summary: Follow-on to #1428. (1) tests/conftest.py: pytest_runtest_setup/teardown hook wrappers record socket.getaddrinfo, socket.create_connection, socket.socket.connect/connect_ex and http.client.HTTPConnection._tunnel, plus airplane's saved _orig_* originals (an uninstall copies those onto socket), before a test and, after every fixture and monkeypatch undo has run, fail the test by name if one is now a callable defined in test code, putting the original back (also when a fixture teardown raised) so one leaker blames one test and not its neighbours. It is a hook wrapper, not an autouse fixture, because monkeypatch can undo after an autouse fixture's teardown; an earlier fixture version blamed 43 tests and desynchronised 11 ssrf tests, and only test-defined callables count. (2) tests/test_entity_spine.py: the airplane test records airplane.is_installed() and the armed flag and puts them back, so it no longer uninstalls a connect guard that an earlier fetch installed. (3) tests/test_event_loop_signal_exemption.py: the child server sets signal.default_int_handler first, because Python 3.13 installs it at start only when SIGINT is not inherited as ignored, which a backgrounded non-interactive shell does; the 60 s health wait is unchanged. Full -n 4 suite: 24,415 passed, 304 skipped, 1 failed (the local-only gzip test, starlette 1.3.1 in the lock).
